strategy.summary: Reproduce the exponnorm small-K cancellation bug (gh-24551, PR gh-24597) by building SciPy at the buggy commit c998b5fcaf06 and running the developer's test_extremely_small_K, which compares exponnorm(K).logpdf, cdf and sf against the standard normal for K in 1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15 using assert_allclose. The test should fail on the buggy build (cdf values are negative/cancelled at K=1e-11 per the issue) and pass on the fixed build.

system_packages: BLAS/LAPACK dev libraries (or use SciPy's bundled OpenBLAS via wheel-style build)
build_commands: git checkout c998b5fcaf06 && git submodule update --init --recursive
pinned_because: numpy 2.4.2 is taken from the reporter's system information in issue#24551; no documented constraint or era ceiling exists, so this is a choice to match the reporter, not a stated requirement
scipy is built from the buggy commit itself rather than pinned to 1.17.0, because the transition must be observed on the source tree under test
python 3.13.11 is from the reporter's environment, also not a documented constraint

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py: test_extremely_small_K (parametrized K=1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15; added after test_sf_small_K in the exponnorm test class)
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit c998b5fcaf06 the test_extremely_small_K cases fail, because assert_allclose on exponnorm cdf/logpdf/sf disagrees with norm at x=[-10.5,-3,-1,1,3,10.5]; on the fixed revision (the PR merge) all three parametrized cases pass. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np; from scipy import stats; x=np.array([-4.,4.]); print(stats.exponnorm(1e-11).cdf(x), stats.norm.cdf(x))"
risks: The bug is numerical cancellation, not platform-specific per the evidence, so it should reproduce on any x86_64 or aarch64 Linux build; no architecture or sanitiser requirement is stated, and none is assumed.

The tolerance is not stated in the evidence. The test uses assert_allclose with no explicit rtol or atol, so its default rtol (1e-7 in numpy) decides the transition; this default is not given in the passages and is relied on from numpy, not from the evidence.

The K threshold changed across commits (1e-9, then 1e-6, then K<1). The fixed revision's behaviour at K=1e-15 depends on which erfcx branch version is merged, so verify the fixed build directly rather than assuming it.

The PR accepts an overflow RuntimeWarning in intermediate calculations. If the pytest configuration turns warnings into errors, the fixed revision may fail for warning reasons, which would break the pass transition; check filterwarnings in the pytest config.

The exact test class name for test_extremely_small_K is inferred from its placement next to test_sf_small_K; -k selection avoids depending on it, but a class-qualified node id would need verification.

Build from source takes substantial time and needs compilers and BLAS/LAPACK; a mismatch between the built SciPy and the numpy version can cause import errors that look like test failures, so confirm the import works before reading the transition.

oracle.reference_source: scipy.stats.norm (standard normal) as the reference in the developer test; mpmath mp.dps=75 reference is used in the PR discussion but not in the reproducing test
oracle.why: The reproducing test compares to norm with assert_allclose defaults; no explicit tolerance is given in the evidence, so the separating tolerance is recorded as null.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion sees exponnorm(K).cdf at x=-4 or -10.5 returning a negative or cancelled value (e.g. -9.99968e-01 where the normal gives 3.16712e-05) at K=1e-11 or 1e-9, far outside the default rtol, so assert_allclose raises AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the erfcx-based branches applied, exponnorm(K) logpdf, cdf and sf match norm to within assert_allclose tolerance for K=1e-9, 1e-12 and 1e-15, so all parametrized cases pass.
